subject: paediatrics
title: Acute Rheumatic Fever, Revised Jones Criteria and Sydenham Chorea

steps.tx: Delayed autoimmune sequelae of pharyngeal streptococcal infection cause multi-system tissue destruction. Occurring two to three weeks following untreated Streptococcus pyogenes pharyngitis, **acute rheumatic fever** (ARF) arises from humoral and cellular cross-reactivity between streptococcal cell wall M-proteins and human host antigens. This molecular mimicry triggers inflammatory damage across cardiac valves, synovial joints, basal ganglia, and subcutaneous connective tissues.
steps.say: Acute rheumatic fever is an autoimmune complication arising weeks after streptococcal pharyngitis. Molecular mimicry between streptococcal M-protein and human tissue damages heart valves, joints, and brain.

vis.alt: Major and minor clinical criteria for the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever.
vis.caption: Revised Jones criteria major manifestations including carditis, arthritis, chorea, and erythema marginatum. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Standardized diagnostic scoring mandates proven antecedent streptococcal exposure alongside clinical criteria. Under the **revised Jones criteria**, establishing a primary diagnosis requires microbiological or serological proof of antecedent Group A streptococcal infection (elevated anti-streptolysin O titer or positive throat culture) accompanied by either two major criteria or one major and two minor criteria. The presence of Sydenham chorea or indolent carditis alone can establish diagnosis without strict criteria fulfillment.
steps.say: Diagnosing acute rheumatic fever requires evidence of preceding streptococcal infection plus two major criteria, or one major and two minor criteria. Sydenham chorea alone can confirm the diagnosis.

steps.tx: Acute valvular regurgitation represents the only manifestation producing permanent, progressive structural morbidity. Clinical or Doppler echocardiographic **rheumatic carditis valvulitis** characteristically targets the mitral valve in over ninety percent of cases, producing acute mitral regurgitation, accompanied by aortic regurgitation in thirty percent. Pathological examination reveals Aschoff nodules in the myocardium and small verrucous vegetations along the lines of valvular closure.
steps.say: Rheumatic carditis is the only manifestation causing permanent damage, primarily causing acute mitral regurgitation and Carey Coombs murmurs. Aschoff nodules form in the myocardium.

vis.alt: Gross pathology of rheumatic heart valve vegetations and thickening.
vis.caption: Verrucous vegetations along lines of mitral valve closure and chordal shortening in rheumatic carditis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Fleeting inflammation of large joints responds with dramatic rapid relief to salicylate pharmacotherapy. The most common presenting manifestation is **migratory polyarthritis**, affecting large joints like knees, ankles, elbows, and wrists in rapid succession. The inflammation characteristically moves from one joint to another over days, with affected joints becoming intensely hot, red, swollen, and exquisitely tender, yet completely resolving without chronic joint deformities.
steps.say: Migratory polyarthritis causes intense pain and swelling moving sequentially between large joints like knees and ankles. It responds dramatically to oral aspirin within forty-eight hours.

left.title: Rheumatic Polyarthritis Features
points: Severe pain out of proportion to swelling
Dramatically resolves with aspirin in 48 hr

right.title: Post-Streptococcal Reactive Arthritis
points: Involves small joints and axial skeleton
Poor, sluggish response to aspirin therapy
Lower risk of progressive rheumatic carditis

steps.tx: Autoimmune targeting of basal ganglia structures produces purposeless involuntary movements and emotional lability. The neurological manifestation **Sydenham chorea St Vitus dance** occurs months after initial streptococcal pharyngitis, caused by autoantibodies binding to striatal dopamine receptors. Patients display continuous, jerky, non-repetitive involuntary movements of the face and limbs, emotional volatility, darting tongue (jack-in-the-box tongue), and milkmaid grip with rhythmic squeezing of fingers.
steps.say: Sydenham chorea causes involuntary purposeless jerky movements, emotional outbursts, and milkmaid grip months after infection. Autoantibodies cross-react with basal ganglia dopamine receptors.

rows: Ask patient to squeeze examiner's fingers
Ask patient to protrude tongue for 20 sec
Inability to maintain sustained motor posture
Bed rest and quiet non-stimulating room

steps.tx: Transient serpiginous erythematous plaques appear primarily across covered trunk and proximal limbs. The dermatological sign **erythema marginatum** manifests as non-pruritic, evanescent, rose-red macules with elevated borders and central clearing, spreading centrifugally in serpentine patterns over the trunk and proximal extremities while completely sparing the face. Lesions wax and wane within hours, becoming prominent with warm baths, accompanied by painless subcutaneous nodules over extensor tendons.
steps.say: Erythema marginatum produces evanescent pink rings with clear centers over the trunk, sparing the face. Firm painless subcutaneous nodules over extensor tendons correlate with severe carditis.

vis.alt: Dermatological manifestations of streptococcal disease showing erythema marginatum rings.
vis.caption: Erythema marginatum with serpentine borders and central clearing alongside subcutaneous nodules. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Structured anti-inflammatory pharmacotherapy suppresses systemic inflammation and relieves disabling joint pain. First-line management for isolated polyarthritis utilizes **oral aspirin therapy** (75 to 100 mg/kg/day divided every six hours for two to three weeks, then tapered). When moderate to severe carditis with cardiomegaly or congestive heart failure is present, oral prednisone (2 mg/kg/day for two to four weeks) is prescribed, followed by gradual taper alongside aspirin to prevent rebound carditis.
steps.say: High-dose oral aspirin treats rheumatic polyarthritis effectively. Moderate or severe carditis with heart failure requires oral corticosteroids tapered over several weeks.

left.title: Aspirin for Arthritis
points: Dose: 75 to 100 mg/kg/day divided 4 times daily
Rapid relief of joint fever and tenderness in 48 hr
Continue for 2 to 3 weeks, then taper over 2 weeks
Monitor for salicylate toxicity and gastritis

right.title: Prednisone for Severe Carditis
points: Oral prednisone (2 mg/kg/day) for 2 to 4 weeks
Indicated for cardiomegaly, pericarditis, heart failure
Add aspirin during steroid taper to prevent rebound
Bed rest until acute phase reactants normalize

steps.tx: Long-term antimicrobial prophylaxis prevents recurrent streptococcal infections that accelerate chronic valvular deformities. Secondary prevention mandates regular **intramuscular benzathine penicillin G** (1.2 million units for children over 27 kg; 600,000 units for smaller children) administered every three to four weeks. In children with established rheumatic carditis and residual valvular disease, prophylaxis must continue for ten years from the last attack or until age forty, and often lifelong.
steps.say: Secondary prevention requires intramuscular benzathine penicillin every three to four weeks. Patients with persistent rheumatic heart disease require prophylaxis for ten years or until age forty.
